title: The affine etale site of an affine formal algebraic space is the category of representable etale affine formal algebraic spaces over it
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the affine etale site of an affine formal algebraic space with the category of morphisms from an affine formal algebraic space into it which are representable by algebraic spaces and etale (statement lines 7479-7491). The proof constructs the equivalence in both directions. The functor takes such a morphism to its fibre product with the reduction of the base, and the first observation is that the morphism is in fact representable by schemes and affine, so that this fibre product is an affine scheme, giving an object of the affine etale site (proof lines 7493-7503). For the quasi-inverse the base is written as a filtered colimit of affine schemes, each of which receives the reduction as a thickening; since etale affine schemes over a scheme depend only on the reduction in this situation, an etale morphism from an affine scheme to the reduction extends to a compatible system of etale morphisms at every stage, whose colimit is an affine formal algebraic space over the base (proof lines 7505-7520). The author then observes that the construction has the expected fibre products along the stages, which shows the resulting morphism is representable and etale, and leaves the verification that the two constructions are mutually inverse to the reader (proof lines 7520-7526). The claim is H2: both functors are built and their required properties -- affineness of the fibre product in one direction, representability and etaleness in the other -- are proved, with only the final round-trip verification omitted.
